findings.code_snippet:
n. Without `--revoke`, removed keys stay authorized on-chain until they expire; `--revoke` revokes them first, on every network the logout covers, and cannot be undone. A retryable `E_USAGE` saying the wallet changed during logout means another login or refresh ran meanwhile, so the wallet may now hold keys the user has not seen. Report it and rerun the logout only after the user approves again; its command keeps `--yes`, so a rerun logs out, and with `--revoke` revokes, the wallet as it now is without asking. If a key is not revoked, logout fails and keeps it with the wallet; report it before retrying.
- Closing a session cannot be undone, and a closed session can no longer pay for requests. Run `tempo wallet sessions close <TARGET> --dry-run` (or with `--all`, `--orphaned`, `--finalize`, or `--cooperative`) to list the sessions it selects as `targets[]`, each with its `channel_id`, `origin`, and `status` (`not_found` when nothing matches), then run its `_next` (which adds `--yes`) on

findings.code_snippet:
- Link keeps one approval policy per app: a Link CLI policy does not cover another client, such as
  a Mercator via Link (`https://mercator.link/mcp`) connection signed in to Link, whose
  `get_connection_status` returns its own `policySetupUrl`. An `approval_policy_not_found` or
  "no approval policy is configured" response means that app has none; offer its policy page.
- Pay from Link Balance first when the account has one (Link CLI: `--payment-method-id` with the
  `BALANCE` method's ID); Link may refuse card-backed SPTs under $0.50. Mercator's managed Link
  payments pick Balance automatically.
